correctness.rationale: For q=ρ⁴/(8D₀), q'=ρ³/(2D₀); the drift of q is 2−α and D(q')²=2q. Under the specified instantaneous zero-flux extension this is BESQ(δ), including δ=1 (instantaneously reflecting) and δ=2 (entrance from zero). Independent Poisson resets give regeneration and a unique stationary law with age Exp(r). The BESQ Laplace transition, checked by the backward equation, has gamma law from 0. Averaging its no-reset term over the stationary state gives the first term of the joint transform; the last-reset integrand is independent of Q₀ and yields the second. The age product yields moments 2^k k!(δ/2)_k/r^k. Finite moments and full support give the orthogonal basis by degree with no completeness assumption in L² needed. The reset generator is triangular on polynomials, with highest coefficient −r for positive degrees. Independently, G P₁=−rP₁ and G P₂=−rP₂+2(δ+2)P₁, using the moment-derived coefficients. Exponentiating that two-dimensional block gives zero reverse covariance and 2(δ+2)Var(Q) t e^(−rt) forward; all the equal-degree normalized correlations follow by degree preservation and orthogonality. The moment and lag formulas invert on δ∈[1,2] and r,D₀>0 at known t>0. No finite-sample claim is supported; the supplied script and its stated diagnostics were read, not executed.
